title: Paper vs. Practice: A Field Investigation of Integrity Hotlines

scopes.description: The documented historical workflow covers selection of 250 firms from the stated possible set of 685 (with an S&P 900 reference as of October 2017), manual hotline-location research, website/email inquiries and response waiting, recording and coding field observations, merging Appendix B controls, and the described t-test, OLS and logistic analyses. The release documents these manual stages but supplies no dataset or executable program. A compatible author-prepared merged dataset may serve as the empirical input and bypass rebuilding historical field contacts. The frame reference does not establish the field-collection period or current index membership.

requirements.description: A company-level empirical dataset compatible with the study, including the recorded field observations (anonymous-reporting text, phone/email/web channel availability, obstacles, provider, inquiry response dates and text), the paper-defined coded outcomes, and the Appendix B controls merged at firm level (examples include revenue and company age). Exact column names, types, coding values, join key, row-level sample identifiers and date coverage are not supplied. A compatible author-prepared dataset is a valid primary input; the datasheet’s 250-of-685 sampling frame and October 2017 S&P 900 reference describe historical frame provenance, not current membership or the field-collection period.

issues.description: No executable analysis or data-preparation program, entry point, or run instructions are included. The datasheet names t-statistics, OLS and logistic regressions but does not identify software, model specifications, commands, or a table-to-analysis mapping. The workflow is partly documented as manual field collection and coding, so this is no runnable code rather than no documented workflow.

The datasheet delegates firm-selection criteria, inquiry creation and sending, and variable definitions to the paper and Appendix B, which are not included in this release. The exact sampled firm identifiers, field-collection dates, coded-variable dictionary, historical manual lookup/crosswalk records, complete control-variable list, merge key, and final data schema therefore remain unspecified. The 250/685 sample-frame count and October 2017 S&P 900 reference do not resolve those details or establish the collection period.

evidence.description: Historical sample frame: 250 selected from 685, with S&P 900 membership dated October 2017.
evidence.quote:
The sample of 250 companies was randomly selected from the possible set of 685 (see criteria
described in the paper). Within the paper, the set of S&P 900 was as of October 2017 (i.e. S&P set
of firms changes over time).

evidence.description: The documented field procedure locates each hotline, sends an inquiry by website or email, and waits for a response.
evidence.quote:
Inquiries for each of the sample companies were sent via their website or e-mail hotline as described
in the paper. In particular, after identifying the location of the helpline (as described in the paper),
research associates sent in the inquiry and waited (according to the methodology in the paper) for a
response.

evidence.description: The datasheet describes t-statistics, OLS and logistic regression, refers coding choices to the paper appendix, and says variables were not further modified or truncated.
evidence.quote:
As readers of the paper will see, the analysis in the paper is econometrically very basic (e.g. t-stats,
OLS, and logistic regressions). Moreover, the choices around coding variables (e.g. definition of
closing an inquiry) are described in detail in the paper’s appendix. Following the aforementioned
data collection, there was no additional modification, selection, or truncation of any variables used in
the dataset (field collection data or control variables collected from archival sources noted in the
paper in Appendix B).

evidence.description: The datasheet lists recorded field variables, paper-defined coding, and merged Appendix B controls including revenue from Compustat.
evidence.quote:
For each company in the sample, the following data fields were recorded: text around anonymous
reporting, availability of phone/e-mail/and web reporting, all obstacles encountered during
reporting process (as displayed in chart), provider, date and text of the response to each inquiry.
Each of these variables was coded according to the specific methodology described in the paper
(with no data points deviating from this process). For each company in the sample, the control
variables were collected and merged with the final dataset as described in the paper (e.g. revenue
from Compustat) with no further modification. There was no transformation or truncation of any
control variables or other data collected from the field research.

actions.description: Resolve the compatible author-prepared empirical input and its schema.
steps: Identify whether an existing author-prepared company-level dataset containing the field records, paper-defined coded outcomes, and merged controls can be obtained through an authorized route; record the route and its access terms before classifying access status.

Obtain the actual file format and data dictionary, including field names, types, units/codes, firm identifier, sample identifiers, inquiry/response date fields, and the Appendix B control variables and merge key. Confirm the data cover the historical study sample described by the authors.

Use the prepared dataset as the input if compatible; do not use current S&P membership or repeat historical hotline contacts to fill missing fields. If no merged dataset exists, clarify the availability of the authors’ existing historical field/coding/control records before assessing any reconstruction route.
validation: After an authorized dataset is available, use a bounded metadata/readability check and compare observed columns, types, keys, date fields, firm coverage and coded values with the supplied dictionary and historical sample identifiers.

Check that field observations and Appendix B controls join on the documented key and that the delivered data preserve the authors’ stated selection and no-additional-truncation process; leave any unsupported schema or coverage claim unresolved.

actions.description: Resolve the missing executable analysis program or complete run recipe.
steps: Obtain the author analysis and data-preparation program(s), or a complete manual/GUI recipe if the authors intentionally did not provide code. Request the actual software and version, entry point and order, input paths/formats, invocation steps, and required outputs.

Obtain the analysis-to-table mapping, including model specifications, outcome and regressor definitions, sample restrictions, and the required t-test, OLS and logistic results; the generic labels in the datasheet do not define these details.
Keep software requirements unassigned until the authors specify them; do not infer Stata, SAS, R, Python, or add-on requirements from the method names alone.
validation: Review the delivered program or recipe against all reported analyses and tables, and trace every input to the resolved dataset or a documented preparation step.

Only in a later authorized execution, run the resolved entry point(s) with the specified software and compare the produced analyses with the paper’s reported outputs; execution is not verified in this assessment.

actions.description: Resolve the manual field, coding, sample and control-variable definitions.
steps: Obtain the full paper and Appendix B or an equivalent author-supplied specification covering the 685-firm eligibility criteria, the historical 250-firm sample identifiers, fieldwork dates, hotline-location lookup, inquiry protocol, response/obstacle coding, and the precise control-variable list and definitions.

Request the final coding dictionary and firm-level merge key, including the stated treatment of inquiry closure and response dates. If the compatible author-prepared dataset is used, use these materials to interpret and validate it; do not rebuild the historical fieldwork or contact sampled companies.

Keep unresolved any sample, coding, timing or control-variable definition that the supplied materials do not establish; do not derive it from the S&P 900 frame reference or the Compustat example alone.
validation: Cross-check every requested field and coded value against the delivered dictionary and prepared data; reconcile control-variable definitions and join keys before analysis.
Confirm the historical selection/frame specification is documented without substituting current index membership, and distinguish sample-frame date from field-collection dates.

review_notes: The frozen work-item dependency checklist is empty, and the package inventory contains only the datasheet; manual collection/coding steps remain part of the documented workflow.
No separate analysis_only scope is supported because no compatible dataset or analysis program is supplied.
The datasheet’s 250-of-685 and October 2017 statements are treated as historical sampling-frame context, not as current firm membership or the study’s collection period.
The frozen title/DOI/provenance are retained even though the datasheet heading uses a variant title and volume/date label.
The data access route and any associated conditions are not stated in the supplied datasheet; the requirement remains undetermined, with no inference of public availability, NDA, or access denial.
No live fieldwork, hotline contact, message, form submission, data acquisition, author-code execution, installation, or source edit was performed.
